What this means

You show up almost everywhere. You rarely win.

You're present in some form across 87.8% of the grid, but only 4.2% of those searches land you in the actual 3-pack people tap on. Performance is strongest to the north and northwest of Oakland, and weakest to the east, south, and southwest. Part of the gap is structural: competitors like STIIIZY San Jose and The Highlands Weed Dispensary and Delivery have "weed delivery" baked directly into their business name, which gives them an algorithmic head start. But there's real opportunity too: rivals like Eaze and Lofi Weed Delivery have strong reviews or ratings and still aren't converting that into map-pack share, and Blaze 420 Weed Delivery currently holds 0% SoLV in this grid. Your 4.8-star rating is an asset you're not using to full effect yet.

AI answer engines: a real edge, with a big asterisk

We ran the same "weed delivery" query across four AI platforms on the same grid. The headline numbers below look great on their own, so here's the honest read before you get excited about them.

Read this first

Most cannabis queries get refused outright, not ranked

Across most of the grid, these AI assistants simply decline to answer "weed delivery" questions at all ("I cannot fulfill requests for recommendations, services, or delivery related to cannabis..."). The "share of voice" numbers below are calculated only over the fraction of searches that actually got an answer, not the full grid. That's why Gemini can show 95.8% and still only have responded to 46 of 361 points. The number that matters most is search presence: how often the assistant answers at all.

The biggest single opportunity

"weed delivery near me" gets 12,000 searches a month. You're on page 3.

It's the highest-volume term on your entire list, and you sit at position 28. "cannabis delivery near me" (7,700/mo) sits at position 17. Neither is close to page one. Moving either into the top 10 would be worth more than most of the smaller city terms combined.
